text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish newspapers this morning.
- Insurer Pohjola's owners come onto its board in organisation reshuffle.
- Consumption feast starting again in Finland, but unlike the previous boom of the late 1980s, only the well off are joining in.
- Computer software updates for the turn of the millenium and preparations for Economic and Monetary Union are estimated to cost billions of markka in Finland. @
- Labour ministry and Statistics Finland jobless data for December showed opposite trends due to exceptionally high distortion from the two authorities' different methods and sample periods.
- Prime minister Paavo Lipponen had fever, cancelled all appointments on Thursday.
- EU to investigate UPM-Kymmene's and Nokia's disposal of Finnish Chemicals to a group of investors in December. @
- The state's and municipalities' corporate tax revenues to rise by 2-3 billion markka this year from 13 billion last year, which was already exceptionally high.
- Unemployment is falling quickly in the construction sector, down 13 percentage points year-on-year in December.
- Risk of punishment minor consideration for burglars, study shows. Only one in 14 sentenced burglars hesitated before the crime for fear of being punished. @
- President Martti Ahtisaari cools speculation that Finland would join NATO, says membership in EMU would also improve security.
